table.title: [Composition of the National Assembly (Revised Regulations of the Tzechengyuan, Clause 10)]
table.caption_extra: Revised Regulations of the Tzechengyuan (sanctioned July 3, 1911), Chapter II.—Members. 10. The composition of the Assembly is :—

rows: Sixteen Members from among the Imperial Princes and Dukes.
Twelve Members from Manchu and Chinese Hereditary Nobles.
Fourteen from the Princes and Dukes of the Dependencies.
Six from the Imperial Clansmen and Gioro.
Ten of those persons who pay large taxes.
One hundred Members of Provincial Assemblies (200 members).

transcriber_notes: Numbered list within Clause 10 transcribed as a table because it gives membership figures; the other sub-lists in the Regulations (Clause 9 classes eligible, Clause 14 matters decided) are part of legal clauses and treated as prose.
Figures printed in words; '(200 members)' printed after class 8: parts 16+12+14+6+32+10+10+100 sum to 200 — reconciles (as the total membership of the Assembly).

table.title: [Imperial Decrees on the subject of missionaries]
table.caption_extra: Imperial Decrees² on the subject of missionaries have been issued as follow:—

rows: Ordering protection to be afforded to foreign missionary establishments.
Ordering protection of missionary establishments and suppression of idle stories and suspicion.
Ordering officials to guard carefully against missionary troubles and to afford “thorough protection to missionaries passing to and fro.”

footnotes: ² See Hertslet's China Treaties, Vol. II.
transcriber_notes: First entry on p. 403, remaining two on p. 404.
